snippet: Inhibrx CEO Mark Lappe was particularly keen on INBRX-106’s performance in patients with HPV-positive disease and sees a nearly $4 billion near-term opportunity thanks to the Phase 2 results.

title: Novo shutters 2 more heart disease studies, indicating IL-6 is ‘invalid target’
snippet: After the failure of Novo Nordisk’s IL-6 inhibitor ziltivekimab sent waves through the industry, the company has terminated two other studies of the asset, bringing the total number of high-profile cardiovascular flops to six over nine weeks.

title: Roivant's pulmonary hypertension drug shines with ‘blowout’ Phase 2 data
snippet: Mosliciguat, being developed by the Roivant Sciences subsidiary Pulmovant, 'significantly exceeded expectations' in reducing pulmonary vascular resistance, according to analysts, and is progressing to a late-stage study.

title: AstraZeneca’s SERD pill overcomes adcomm defeat to win FDA nod in breast cancer
snippet: The approval opens up a “modest” market for AstraZeneca’s Etcamah, according to Leerink analysts, who nevertheless looked forward to an upcoming late-stage readout that could lead to a “significantly larger opportunity” for the drug.

title: Novartis’ $12B Avidity acquisition hits Phase 3 speedbump as dystrophy drug disappoints
snippet: While Novartis’ antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate failed to significantly improve hand function in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1, the asset nevertheless showed signs of clinical activity in secondary and exploratory measures.

title: Moonwalk pulls in $70M to take fat-targeting RNAi obesity candidate to clinic
snippet: Moonwalk Biosciences plans to shepherd its lead obesity asset into first-in-human trials in late 2027. In preclinical studies, MW101 has demonstrated weight loss and fat reduction while maintaining muscle mass.

title: Novartis’ cholesterol-lowering medicine fails Phase 3, clouding Lp(a) horizons
snippet: The failure of Novartis’ pelacarsen to translate its Lp(a)-lowering effects to clinical benefits “marks a meaningful setback” for other companies taking a similar approach to cardiovascular risk, analysts say—including Eli Lilly and Amgen.
